findings.source: main.sol:917-982 getVaultLiquidation: uint vaultType_ = getVaultType(vault_); if (vaultType_ != 0) { ... } (one body after the call)
findings.issue: getVaultType has four exits with different vaultType_ values (TYPE() result, multi-byte and 1-byte address checks, id 0); the whole continuation is printed once per exit, so getVaultLiquidation is 2,900 lines for ~70 source lines and the two wrappers repeat it again. getVaultEntireData merges only after 1,500 duplicated lines (at 6162).
findings.rule: When several paths reach the same code and differ only in the values of some variables, print that code once after the join and give the differing values a variable assigned in each path (a phi), instead of tail-duplicating it.

findings.issue: x = c and 10000 can only be 0 or 10000, so under 'if x:' (or after 'if not x: return/continue') the test 'x != 10000' is false and its 50-line arm (the non-T1 constantsView decode) is dead, yet it is printed 22 times.
findings.rule: Track the value set of 'c and K' (K a nonzero constant) as {0, K}; under a test that excludes 0 the variable equals K, so comparisons with K fold and the dead arm is dropped.

findings.source: addressCalcs.sol:20-31 keccak256(abi.encodePacked(bytes1(0xd6), bytes1(0x94), deployedFrom_, uint8(nonce_))); helpers.sol:31 require(tickRaw_ < X20, "invalid-number"); main.sol:196 return AddressCalcs.addressCalc(...)
findings.issue: The cause of P2 also hides other effects: the RLP keccak is a sha3 over a memory buffer whose length reads '_26 - mem[64] + 27' (=27), the tick check's revert reason 'invalid-number' is shown only as hex bytes and 'revert with memory', and returns are memory ranges with symbolic lengths. Where the same code runs at a constant address (getVaultType 507, getVaultState 330, getVaultAddress 256) it is folded to sha3(Bytes(22, ...), ...) and revert with 'invalid-number'.
findings.rule: Bound the free-memory word: if every value stored at mem[64] is a constant >= 96 plus nonnegative sizes kept below 2^64 by the Panic(65) checks, writes at mem[64] + k (k >= 0) cannot alias the word at 64, so 'v = mem[64]' re-read after them is v, '_26 - mem[64]' is 0, and the buffer, revert and return are resolved as at constant addresses.

findings.rule: A read of mem[b + k .. b + k + 32) inside a region written by 'mem[b len min(n, return_data.size)] = ext_call.return_data[0 len ...]', under a dominating return_data.size >= k + 32 and k + 32 <= n, is ext_call.return_data[k]; mem[a + 12 len 20] of a known word w is address(w).

findings.source: main.sol:242-249 uint16(vaultVariables2_ & X16) ...; :300-305 supplyRateVault = int256((supplyRateMagnifier >> 1) & X15); if (...) supplyRateVault = -supplyRateVault; tickMath.sol:45 absTick_; main.sol:811 owner
findings.issue: The same field extraction is printed as a byte slice in one line and as a mask/shift in the next; the checked negation keeps its int256.min test although the operand is below 2^15; TickMath's absTick_ is recomputed in each of 15 tests with a no-op int24() of a 19-bit value; an address in a return is split into two byte items.
findings.rule: Print a byte slice of a word with a known value v as the equivalent shift/mask of v; fold a comparison that the operand's known range makes false (x < 2^15 is never 2^255); bind a subexpression used more than twice to a temporary; drop intN(x) when x is known to fit.

notes: Reviewed against main.sol / helpers.sol and the libraries. The functions over 1,500 lines (getVaultLiquidation, getVaultEntireData, getMultipleVaultsLiquidation, getAllVaultsLiquidation, getVaultsEntireData x2, positionByNftId, positionsByUser) were reviewed by structure: control flow, loops, calls, reverts, returns; getVaultLiquidation's T1 and non-T1 try/catch blocks, the _decodeLiquidationResult copies (selector 0xcc36aa44, amtOut at +36, amtIn at +68, Error(string) and decode-failure fallbacks), _getVaultConstants (both struct layouts, field by field), _getVaultConfig, _getExchangePricesAndRates, _getTotalSupplyAndBorrow, the withdrawal-limit block of _getLimitsAndAvailability, getVaultState, getVaultType, TickMath.getRatioAtTick and positionByNftId's vaultType==0 path (amounts become 0 through the zero exchange prices, fetchLatestPosition's supply store correctly dropped) were checked line by line. getVaultsEntireData x2 and positionsByUser are the same inlined getVaultEntireData / positionByNftId bodies inside their loops; getVaultsAbsorb() = getVaultsAbsorb(address[]) after the getAllVaultsAddresses loop. The only missing extcodesize check (first simulateLiquidate call, 1820) is implied by the dominating 'if ext_code.size(_param1)' with only static calls between, so it is exact; the merge of the two BITS_USER_*_AMOUNT branches is exact (both constants are 1). Loops: 8 source for-loops (main.sol 182, 784, 795, 878, 902, 1012, 1024, 1050) all shown as while (inlined copies of 182 and 878 too); implicit: 4 memory copies as while (P7: getDeploymentName x2, uint[] and address[] encodes), 8 zero-initialisations of new struct[] rotated as 'while idx - 1' (P3), 3 calldata address[] decodes and 8 struct-array encodes as readable whiles. P1: the pack header has no P1 count, but 16 lines print the TYPE() selector as 0x8df3dc...000 * 24 * 3600. P11 includes ~40 in-loop Panic(50) checks implied by the loop bound (the tokensInAmt_[i] check in getMultipleVaultsLiquidation is real), 'if not _param2' after '_386 = ... or not _param2' (1250), '-(d) + b > b' after 'b > d', and the 22 dead blocks of the second finding. P12: the low-level catch block (_decodeLiquidationResult) is printed in 4-5 arms of each try. No execution run: no semantic suspicion remained after reading.
summary: Faithful on every path read, with all 8 loops present, but very bloated: getVaultType's four exits make the decompiler duplicate whole continuations (4 x 700 lines per liquidation body) including 22 provably dead 50-line arms, and memory at the free pointer stays unresolved, so 295 calls lose their names and arguments and keccaks, revert reasons and returns read as raw memory.
